title: Basie's 1950 offer of $135 a week
summary: Basie wanted him for a new small band; Gus bargained from $125 to $135, ten dollars above the others.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And so when he got Butch, well, they came back in town, and I was playing with Cootie's band at the Savoy again. And so he came by the Savoy and told me he wanted to talk to me.
Couldn't get somebody else to do his dirty work, huh?
No. He said, "I want to talk to you on
your intermission." So I said okay. So he said he wanted me back in the band because he was going to start a small band. Now, this was 1950, when he started the small band, see.
So I said, "Well, that all depends on what you're going to pay."

Yeah, the bread at that time. Well, the guys wasn't getting that much, anyway. So he said, "Well, I'll give you $125 a week." I said, "Uh-uh." I said, "No, thanks, anyway. I'm working here at the Savoy with Cootie's band, anyhow, so -- and I just turned around and walked away. And he said, "Well, wait a minute, now," one of those things.

And so he came back and he said, "I'll give you $135." Well, that -- I know what the guys were getting in the band. They weren't getting no more than $125. See, I knew that. So that was ten dollars more than the rest of the guys.
So I said, "Well, I'll let you know, just like that. And so after that, he called me up and he said, "Well, what do you say?" I said, "Okay, I'll make it with you." And he started the small band.
